newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm on strong overnight crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm on strong overnight crude gains.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market soared on Wednesday following overnight rebounds in crude values and strong anticipation that a local trading company will continue pricing up, traders said.
Bids for the 180-cst grade from the local trader inched up to $103 per tonne for early to middle April lifting from an initial $100 per tonne but sellers were sidelines awaiting further price hikes.
The 180-cst was bid at $100 and offered at $101 on Tuesday.
"Suppliers are waiting for the local trader to offer higher bids, which is very likely," said one trader.

Fuel oil swaps also continued their recent strength on the back of crude gains, with April and May jumping to $103.00/$104.00 and $101.00/$102.00 respectively from Tuesday's $99.50/$100.50 and $98.25/$99.50.
Recent market strength was largely boosted by the local trading company which has been heavily buying up the gas oil market and supporting fuel oil prices.
"Supplies are sufficient but demand did not pick up. Fuel oil prices should rise with crude but should not go up that much," said one trader.
"But the market now depends largely on what the local trader will do next," he added.
The firm cargo prices also prompted bunker suppliers to raise their offers but shipowners stayed away from the market, reluctant to pay high prices.
High cargo prices in Singapore have attracted some 250,000 tonnes of arbitrage cargoes to head eastwards, mainly to Singapore, from the Mediterranean since early March, European traders have said.
Some majors have built up stocks in their oil terminals after high prices scared buyers away, traders said.
"Arbitrage cargoes are coming in now and then but enquiries did not increase," said one trader.
In the LSWR market, demand remained slack from Japan though the strong crude helped sentiment slightly, traders said.
